questions.question: The <!______ html> declaration comes first in every HTML document.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <!DOCTYPE html> is the document type declaration that tells browsers this is an HTML5 document. It must be the very first thing in your HTML file.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <!DOCTYPE html> is the document type declaration that tells browsers this is an HTML5 document. It must be the very first thing in your HTML file.

questions.question: The ______ tag is the root element of an HTML page.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <html> tag is the root element - it contains ALL other HTML elements. Think of it as the foundation of your webpage.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <html> tag is the root element - it contains ALL other HTML elements. Think of it as the foundation of your webpage.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <head> section contains metadata - information about the page that isn't displayed, like the title, character set, and links to CSS files.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <head> section contains metadata - information about the page that isn't displayed, like the title, character set, and links to CSS files.

questions.question: Visible content goes inside the ______ section.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <body> section contains EVERYTHING users see on your webpage: text, images, buttons, videos - all the visible content!

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <body> section contains EVERYTHING users see on your webpage: text, images, buttons, videos - all the visible content!

questions.question: HTML stands for Hyper ______ Markup Language.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The 'Text' in HTML refers to hypertext - text that can contain links to other documents. This is what makes the web interconnected!

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The 'Text' in HTML refers to hypertext - text that can contain links to other documents. This is what makes the web interconnected!

questions.question: The page title goes between <title> and </title> tags inside the ______ section.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <title> tag always goes inside the <head> section, not the <body>. This keeps metadata separate from visible content.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <title> tag always goes inside the <head> section, not the <body>. This keeps metadata separate from visible content.

questions.question: HTML uses ______ brackets to define tags.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: HTML tags are always surrounded by angle brackets: < and >. Like this: <html>, <body>, etc.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: HTML tags are always surrounded by angle brackets: < and >. Like this: <html>, <body>, etc.

questions.question: After <!DOCTYPE html>, the next tag should be ______.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The correct order is: <!DOCTYPE html> → <html> → <head> → <body>. The <html> tag wraps everything else.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The correct order is: <!DOCTYPE html> → <html> → <head> → <body>. The <html> tag wraps everything else.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <body> always comes after the <head> in proper HTML structure. Inside <html>, first comes <head>, then <body>.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <body> always comes after the <head> in proper HTML structure. Inside <html>, first comes <head>, then <body>.

questions.question: Content in the <head> is ______ to webpage visitors.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Content in <head> is invisible to regular visitors! It's only visible in browser tabs (title), source code, or to search engines.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Content in <head> is invisible to regular visitors! It's only visible in browser tabs (title), source code, or to search engines.
